requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. I did not read the code that builds the detail plan or calls `replace_definitions`; I relied on the passing tests for that wiring. **Obligations, code and tests** 1. **Definition badge links to the detail page.** - Code: `replace_definitions` in `src/lib.rs` computes `detail_href` from `plan.detail_path`. It emits the badge as an ``. `DetailPlan::detail_path` and `chapter_href` support it. - Test: `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` asserts `id="habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}" href="…"` for a requirement, an example and a name containing `.md`. 2. **Each rendered requirement and example is followed by a "See evidence" link.** - Code: `replace_definitions` appends `

See evidence

`. This applies to every non-term definition that has a detail page. - Test: the same test asserts that link for all three definitions and that "See evidence" appears exactly 3 times. 3. **Detail page links back to the definition's anchored badge.** - Code: `render_detail_page` builds `[View definition](chapter_href(detail_path, definition.path, Some(kind.anchor(name))))`. `DefinitionKind::anchor` builds the anchor. - Tests: `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` asserts `[View definition](../rules.html#habeas-req-rules.zeta)`. The index test asserts `../core.html#habeas-req-requirements.core.ready`. 4. **Detail page links to the index when one exists.** - Code: `render_detail_page` adds `[Requirements index](…)` only when `index_path` is `Some`. - Tests: the index test asserts `[Requirements index](../../appendix/requirements-index.html) · [View definition]`. The no-index test asserts "Requirements index" is absent. 5. **Reference badges continue to link to the definition.** - Code: `reference_badge` and `replace_inline_references` link to the definition's path and anchor via `chapter_href`. - Test: `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` asserts `href="../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.ready"` for impl, cite and test references. 6. **Links resolve when a name contains `.md`.** - Code: `chapter_href` replaces `.md` with `%2Emd` in the generated URL. - Tests: `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` covers both the detail link and the definition link. The `cli.mdbook` case in the no-index test also covers it. **Marking and unspecified behavior** - The relevant code items carry `{impl}` references to `requirements.index.navigation`, and the tests carry `{test}` references. - I found no unmarked implementation and no unspecified behavior. The "View definition" and "Requirements index" link texts and the "See evidence" paragraph fall within what the requirement describes.
